name: Herodian
overview: Herodian is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament as a kinsman of the Apostle Paul. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture provides no additional personal details or tribal affiliations. His mention is brief but highlights his association with Paul within the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name Herodian is presented simply as a proper name in the biblical text without any given meaning or divine origin. There are no additional titles or meanings associated with his name in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Herodian beyond his identification as a kinsman of Paul. No other relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Herodian's significance lies primarily in his connection to Paul, indicating he was part of the Apostle's extended family network. This relationship suggests he was likely involved in the early Christian community, possibly supporting Paul's ministry. Although brief, his mention in Romans 16:11 underscores the importance of familial ties within the early Church.
